clue.text: Display list of 16

definitions.meaning: to display a feeling is to show it plainly, make it evident
a ship's cargo list, the document recording everything in the load named at 16

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on show an inventory of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 16 Down, SHIPLOAD; the second definition is the cargo document carried for it.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means make plain or evident; as a noun it is the shipping document itemising a vessel's cargo.

clue.text: A penny comb, perhaps, for woman's head

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given may be arranged another way

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A cheap comb might do for a lady's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A frilled cotton cap of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, worn indoors by women over their hair.

clue.text: Two little boys committed robbery

parts.note: Nick, a short form of Nicholas
Ed, a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A pair of young lads carried out a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two little boys' supplies two shortened boys' names, NICK and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this verb for stealing, so it fits having committed a theft.

clue.text: Flier with rations for army at war?

definitions.meaning: a bird, a member of the thrush family
food eaten by troops on campaign, out on the battlefield

explanation.surface: Something that flies, eating what soldiers eat on campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A large thrush that winters in Britain; and, split, the food served to troops on campaign.

clue.text: Wanting teachers without big rods?

definitions.meaning: lacking enough employees, such as a school's teaching staff
having only short staffs rather than long poles

explanation.surface: A school lacking teachers and long canes to keep order.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking sufficient employees; and, literally, having only short sticks or poles.

clue.text: Social gathering, not abroad

definitions.meaning: a reception held in one's own house for visitors
staying in one's own country or house rather than away

explanation.surface: A party that takes place in one's own country.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for an informal party hosted in a private house; also the phrase for being in one's own country or dwelling.

clue.text: Saw parts with power to achieve desired effect

definitions.meaning: the cutting points along a saw's blade
force or effectiveness, as in a law with real bite

explanation.surface: Some components of a tool, together with the force to get results.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw blade's points are so called, and the word is also an idiom for real force or bite.

clue.text: From collaborator I ordered musical piece

indicators.note: From tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A partner in a project orders a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large-scale choral composition on a sacred theme, such as Handel's Messiah, is a musical work.

clue.text: One who can interpret power

definitions.meaning: someone who expounds or explains ideas, or performs a work
in mathematics, the index showing how many times a number is multiplied by itself

explanation.surface: Someone able to explain things, possessing authority.
explanation.definitionFit: An expounder or interpreter of ideas, and in algebra the index to which a number is raised.

clue.text: Composer with part brought back for single person

parts.note: J. S. Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: brought back tells us to read the word for part from right to left

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: A composer gets a part returned to him, for some unmarried individual.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man is described by this word, so it stands for a single person.

clue.text: Leave often partly linked with aide

definitions.meaning: to clear off, depart suddenly
the phrase aide-..., a military officer's assistant, ends in these letters, so they are often joined to aide

explanation.surface: A frequently-heard instruction to depart, attached to an assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: An aide-de-camp is an officer's personal assistant; the second half of that title, written as one word, also means to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack up and depart quickly, as an army striking camp; and the tail of the title aide-de-camp.

clue.text: Influence to get the woman to cooperate

parts.note: pull means influence, as in having pull with someone
taken as written
taken as written
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Using one's clout to persuade a woman to work together.
explanation.definitionFit: To work as a team, combining efforts, is to cooperate.

clue.text: Start or finish in Amsterdam? Correct

indicators.note: the start of the city's name, its opening pair of letters, is all that is kept

parts.note: a finish is an end

explanation.surface: A question of whether one begins or ends a trip in Amsterdam, followed by a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening pair of Amsterdam, AM, is also its closing pair, hence 'Start or finish'; add END for 'finish'.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a text is to revise it, to make changes that put it right.

clue.text: Get to ground and score

definitions.meaning: what an aircraft does on landing
in American football, carrying the ball over the opponents' goal line scores points

explanation.surface: Reach the ground and make a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft landing is described this way, and in American and rugby football it names grounding the ball for a score.

clue.text: Indenting for mixed ices? Not at all

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of the following words are jumbled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether ices are blended into an indentation, answered with a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' scrambles the twelve letters of ICES plus NOT AT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Battlements on a castle wall, the alternating notches and raised sections of a parapet, form an indented line.

clue.text: Accountant raised capital for theatrical buildings

parts.note: an auditor is an accountant who checks books

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters go upwards, so they read in reverse

parts.note: capital as an exclamation means excellent, A1, written here with I for the figure 1

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper lifted some funds to pay for theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means first-rate, A1, written AI; 'raised' turns it upward in this down clue to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin-derived word for a hall where an audience sits, so it covers theatres and concert halls.

clue.text: Beginning to pack, a hold is organized for this

definitions.text: Beginning to pack, a hold is organized for this

indicators.note: organized tells us the letters collected are arranged into a fresh order
the beginning of the word pack, its first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: Someone starts packing, and a cargo hold is arranged to take this much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to' takes P from 'pack'; 'organized' shuffles it with A HOLD IS. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The entire cargo a vessel carries is packed into its hold, which is what the clue as a whole pictures.

clue.text: Infant poet

definitions.meaning: a baby still fed at the breast
Sir John ..., the seventeenth-century English Cavalier poet

explanation.surface: A baby who writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An unweaned baby or young animal; and Sir John, the Cavalier poet who wrote lyric verse.

clue.text: Manor, perhaps, or other place

definitions.meaning: a manor house is an example of a home belonging to a nobleman
MPs in the Commons traditionally refer to Parliament's upper chamber as 'the other place'

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between a country estate and somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament, members of each chamber politely call the other chamber 'the other place'.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer's residence fits the words literally, and Westminster's upper chamber is nicknamed 'the other place' by the Commons.

clue.text: Nothing original about rocket exhibited

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: about means the word for original goes around the rocket

parts.note: new means original, novel
the V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, written here VI

explanation.surface: A rocket with nothing novel about it goes on show.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 'doodlebug' was a German flying bomb of 1944, so a Roman-looking V-one stands for a rocket here.
explanation.definitionFit: Things being displayed for the public to see are exhibited.

clue.text: Some time after. Easter near northern resort

parts.note: Whit, or Whitsun, the Christian festival of Pentecost seven weeks after Easter
by means near, beside

explanation.surface: A trip some weeks after Easter to a seaside town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitsun is the British name for Pentecost, seven weeks after Easter. The answer is a seaside town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal town in North Yorkshire, England, famous for its abbey and Dracula links, is a seaside holiday spot.

clue.text: Pet housed in capital surroundings

definitions.meaning: a toy dog breed kept as a pet
of or belonging to Peking, the old name of China's capital

explanation.surface: A pet animal kept in metropolitan conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: Peking is the old Western name of Beijing; the dog breed takes its name from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A small long-haired lapdog breed from China, and also the adjective for things belonging to Peking, China's capital.

clue.text: Row North on French river

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the Oise is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: An argument up north on the bank of a river in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhymes with cow, is a loud din or commotion, which is a racket of sound.

clue.text: Bad smell when head's cut off this fish

indicators.note: the head of the word for a bad smell, its first letter, is removed

parts.note: a stench is a bad smell

explanation.surface: A fish gives off a foul smell once its head has been chopped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater carp-family species found in European ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Method of transferring money back, in the beginning

indicators.note: back tells us to write the money-transfer word in reverse order

parts.note: giro is a bank or post-office system for transferring money between accounts, familiar in Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A money transfer system that goes back to the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: Giro is a British banking system for sending money directly between accounts; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The point where something starts or arises is its source or beginning.

clue.text: Political reformer in church, skilled performer

parts.note: an artist is a skilled performer

explanation.surface: A political campaigner who doubles as an accomplished entertainer in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chartists were a British working-class movement of the 1830s and 1840s campaigning for the People's Charter.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the People's Charter, which demanded votes for working men, was a campaigner for political reform.

clue.text: Level achieved by successful learner

definitions.meaning: a step on a scale, as in a high level of skill
a qualification awarded to a student who passes university studies

explanation.surface: A standard reached by a student who has done well.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade or step on a scale; and the academic qualification a university awards a graduate.

clue.text: Years of melody from this source in New York

definitions.text: Years of melody from this source in New York

parts.words: Years of melody from this source in New York
parts.note: a Manhattan street whose theatres have supplied decades of musicals and show tunes

explanation.surface: Decades of tunes have come from one place in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manhattan avenue lined with theatres is famous for producing stage musicals over many years.
